newsitem.title: UK: Britain gives banker top private finance job.
newsitem.headline: Britain gives banker top private finance job.

text.p: Britain on Monday announced the appointment of Adrian Montague, co-head of global project finance at Dresdner Kleinwort Benson, as chief executive of the Treasury's Private Finance Initiative (PFI) taskforce.

Paymaster General Geoffrey Robinson said Montague, 49, would join the Treasury on August 15. The taskforce was established after a recent review to revive the ailing PFI, which was set up in 1992 by the previous Conservative government.

PFI was aimed at getting private sector funding for major public projects such as hospitals, transport schemes and prisons. But it has been criticised for inneficiency and a failure to consider projects properly before putting them out to tender.
Robinson said the taskforce would be the focal point for PFI and other public/private partnerships.
Montague's responsibilities include signing off the commercial viability of all significant projects which enter procurement in the next two years.
